London, 29<sup>th</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**The U.S. Treasury Department** has reached a tentative debt-reduction agreement with Chrysler’s main creditors but still must get other lenders to sign on for the deal to take effect.  The accord with JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley would reduce Chrysler’s $6.9 billion debt to $2 billion. For the deal to become formal, all of Chrysler’s lenders have to agree.  The group, comprised of about 45 banks and hedge funds, has until Thursday to agree. It still isn’t clear if Chrysler will file for bankruptcy protection.  Under the tentative agreement, bondholders would not get any equity in the company. They had asked for 40 percent as recently as Friday.  But the Treasury did yield by agreeing to have Chrysler repay the $2 bn debt in cash rather than allowing the car maker to keep the debt on its books.  It is not yet clear what schedule Chrysler will have to meet in repaying the debt, and how much if any of the repayment will be covered by the government. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**The National Automobile Dealers Association** , bracing for a possible General Motors bankruptcy, is asking dealers to contribute to a legal fund to protect their interests.  NADA, with the GM National Dealer Council, sent retailers a memo asking them to sign an agreement to hire lawyers and contribute $2,000 for each of their GM stores. NADA may later ask each participant to contribute an additional $1,000 for each location. The appeal was made before Monday’s announcement that GM plans to shrink its U.S. dealer network by half. A similar letter was sent to Chrysler dealers the same day. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Toyota’s** North American auto plants are warehousing key parts to safeguard against supply chain interruptions caused by supplier failures.  It is also looking for duplicate sources of some parts. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Honda** has recently completed the construction of a new engine plant to supply cylinder blocks and casting parts for its 2.2-litre diesel engines in European models. The manufacturing facility, at Ogawa in Japan, will start production in autumn this year.  The plant has only one production line, but this ‘Advanced Flexible Line’ can produce eight different types of engine. _Source:  Honda_ 

**Anooraq** said discussions with Anglo Platinum regarding the purchase of a 51% interest in South Africa’s Lebowa platinum mine, was progressing well and expected to be concluded shortly.  Anooraq was also in discussions with Angloplat to acquire an additional 1% controlling interest in each of the Ga-Phasha, Boikgantsho and Kwanda JV projects.  Anooraq has also renewed its mandate with Standard Chartered Bank to provide a portion of the financing required for implementation of the proposed transaction. The SCB facility being contemplated was a senior debt-term facility in an amount of R750 million. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Corning’s*

* revenues for Q109 declined 9% sequentially to US$989 million, but it expects that continued strengthen in the LCD TV market will boost glass demand in Q209.  Q1 gross margin was 27%, slightly lower than Q4 gross margin of 28%.  Sales in the display technologies segment were US$357 million, down 8% sequentially. Display technologies combined LCD glass volume, including Corning’s wholly owned business and Samsung Corning Precision Glass (SCP), increased 4% sequentially. Volume in the company’s wholly owned business was down 1% sequentially, while SCP’s volume was up c.7%.  The company increased its estimate for the 2009 LCD glass market from two billion square feet to a range of 2.1 billion to 2.2 billion square feet. The change was driven by stronger-than-anticipated demand for LCD TVs, offset slightly by weaker-than-expected demand for notebook computers. The company now expects LCD TV units to grow 18% this year versus its original expectation of 9%. _Source:  Digitimes_
